subject: EdgePay - requested concurrency & burst matrix for reserved clusters
messages:

Subject: Traffic snapshot + ask: sizing guidance for reserved clusters

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this — attached is a short traffic snapshot for our authentication and recommendations flows (edgepay_traffic_snapshot_Q2.csv). Quick summary:
- Baseline average concurrency across all customers: ~150 concurrent requests
- Typical peak (weekday 9am-11am PT): sustained 900-1,200 concurrent requests for ~20-40 minutes
- Short micro-bursts (fraud checks, promo blasts): up to ~3,000 concurrent for 5-15s
- Prompt/response sizes (median): prompt 110 tokens, response 220 tokens; 95th percentile response tokens ~680 tokens
- Expected latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms for auth flow (we can tolerate p99 spikes to 500ms if required)

We're evaluating reserved capacity (monthly commit) and would like your recommendation for:
1) Number of GPUs to reserve for production (targeting the auth & recommendations flows)
2) Suggested burst policy (how much short-term headroom to allow without cold fallback)
3) Any model/quantization recommendations given our 95th token lengths and latency SLO

Can you also confirm whether your sizing assumes heavy KV cache reuse for repeat tokens (our traffic has high repetition for auth prompts)?

Appreciate any initial guidance — if it helps, we can schedule a 30-min workshop later this week.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Chen

Thanks Alex — got the CSV, helpful snapshot. A few clarifying questions before we size anything: 

1) For the "short micro-bursts" (3,000 concurrent for 5-15s), are those global across a single region or could they span multiple regions?
2) Do the auth prompts include any PII-sensitive fields that would prevent using quantized models or cross-region caching?
3) For the 95th-percentile response token length (~680), is that mostly outliers (e.g., expanded explanations) or do you see many requests at that scale?
4) What's your target availability window for canary fails — i.e., do you need instant failover to hosted variants or is a 10s fallback acceptable?

Karthik — can you glance at the CSV and advise whether a 3x baseline burst vs a configured microburst policy makes more sense given these token sizes?

Happy to take this into a quick sizing workshop — I've penciled in 30 minutes tomorrow at 10:00 PT but can move if that doesn't work.

On Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 11:03 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Karthik — can you glance at the CSV and advise whether a 3x baseline burst vs a configured microburst policy makes more sense given these token sizes?

Quick pass from my side after a 30-min look at the CSV and token distribution:
- The traffic shows strong prefix reuse for auth (good for KV cache). We should count on high cache hit-rate which materially reduces per-token compute for repeated flows.
- 95p token = 680 is in the long-tail; auth flow p95 is ~240 tokens. The large 680-token responses are for a small subset (recommendations / diagnostics). Treat them as separate workload.

Sizing guidance (initial hypothesis):
- Baseline (steady-state): size for 200 concurrent auth requests (safe buffer above 150). With KV caching and gpt-style transformer quantized to int8 (we can discuss quantization risk with EdgePay), estimate ~12-14 requests/s per A100-equivalent GPU at median token footprint (prompt+response ~350 tokens).
- Sustained peak (20-40m window): design reserved pool to handle 1,000 concurrent (not full 1,200 unless you want to suppress hosted fallback for longer windows). That maps to roughly 70–90 A100-equivalent GPU-minutes depending on batching efficiency — roughly 8–10 GPUs to cover sustained peak with autoscaling buffers.
- Micro-bursts (5–15s, up to 3,000 concurrent): use a burst policy that allows up to ~3x the sustained peak for very short windows (10–30s) but rely on hosted fallback for anything beyond that. Allowing 3x sustained for <30s reduces dropped requests while keeping committed capacity reasonable.

Operational notes:
- Enable KV prefix caching for auth to reduce token compute (we'll provide recommended cache TTLs).
- Use batch size caps at request time to maintain <200ms p95 latency; we should simulate batching impact with your real traffic.
- If EdgePay is comfortable with int8 quantization and we've validated quality on a small evalset, we can reduce GPU count by ~20–30% vs fp16.

I'll draft a compact sizing matrix and costs if you want — Dev, can you assemble a quick proposed reserved-sku + burst policy spreadsheet we can share?

--
Karthik Iyer
Staff ML Engineer, Inference Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed reserved sizing + burst policy (attached)

Hi Alex / team — attaching a concise proposal (proposed_reserved_sizing.xlsx) based on Karthik's hypothesis and Mina's clarifying questions. TL;DR:

- Recommended reserved fleet: 9 x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated) for primary region
- Auto-burst policy: allow up to 3x sustained capacity for 30s windows (burst tokens billed at hosted fallback rates if exceeded)
- Microburst guardrails: allow up to 10x sustained for <10s but only best-effort (may hit hosted fallback)
- Model variant: rdx-open-13B-int8 (recommended) with a fallback to rdx-open-13B-fp16 hosted endpoint for critical 95p workloads during very large bursts
- Estimated monthly committed token capacity: 2.8B tokens (with projection notes in sheet)

Action items for EdgePay to proceed:
1) Confirm whether quantized int8 model is acceptable for recommendation outputs (we'll run a short eval).
2) Sign the NDA (if you haven't) so we can share internal benchmark artifacts.
3) Book a 60-min workload workshop so we can simulate your CSV and finalize batching/latency knobs.

Related links: HubSpot deal EDG-2027-0417 (https://hubspot.example/deals/EDG-2027-0417) — I've added the proposed sizing sheet to the deal record.

If that aligns, we'll prepare the formal reserved quote and a rollout plan (canary -> full rollover).

Thanks,
Dev Patel
